answer: To resist Sybil attacks, autonomous agents stake verifiable credentials, forcing attackers to lock massive capital across each knoll, rendering expected utility strictly negative; slashing misbehavior triggers immediate stake loss, a credible deterrent. This economic cost sustains a robust equilibrium where honest agents outcompete malicious actors, preserving Byzantine fault tolerance as the cryptographic lattice—like a crystal—rigidly resists adversarial wander.
